title: Amazing animals of Kazakhstan
paragraphs: Kazakhstan is one of the most biodiverse countries in Central Asia. Its vast territory — the ninth largest in the world — includes steppes, deserts, mountain ranges, forests, and wetlands, each home to a remarkable variety of wildlife. Many of Kazakhstan's native animals are among the most endangered species on the planet, making conservation efforts here critically important. In this article, we explore five of the most fascinating animals that call Kazakhstan home.

The snow leopard is perhaps the most iconic and mysterious wild cat in Central Asia. Known as "irbis" in Kazakh, it lives in the highest and most remote mountain ranges of southeastern Kazakhstan, particularly the Tian Shan and Altai ranges. Snow leopards are perfectly adapted to their extreme environment: they have the thickest fur of any wild cat, the longest tail for balance on rocky terrain, and enormous paws that act as natural snowshoes. Fewer than 4,000 snow leopards remain in the wild worldwide, and Kazakhstan is home to an estimated 150–200 of them.

The saiga antelope is one of the oldest and strangest-looking animals on the steppe. With its peculiar, bulbous nose — which acts as a natural air filter and temperature regulator in the extreme steppe climate — the saiga looks almost like a creature from another era. And indeed it is: the saiga is older than the woolly mammoth, having roamed the Eurasian steppe for more than 2 million years. Kazakhstan is home to the largest population of saiga antelope in the world, with nearly 1 million individuals — a remarkable conservation success story after the species nearly went extinct in the 1990s.

The steppe eagle is one of the most powerful birds of prey in the region. With a wingspan of up to 2.1 metres, it is one of the largest eagles in the world. Steppe eagles are extraordinary hunters: they can spot prey from a height of 600 metres and dive at speeds of up to 250 kilometres per hour. They nest on the open steppe and feed primarily on rodents, reptiles, and carrion. Unfortunately, the steppe eagle is classified as endangered: its population has declined by more than 90% in the last fifty years due to habitat loss and poisoning from pesticides.

The Caspian seal is the world's smallest and most isolated marine mammal. Found exclusively in the Caspian Sea — the world's largest lake — this charming animal lives nowhere else on Earth. Caspian seals have the most expressive dark eyes of any seal species, and their pups are covered in the whitest, softest fur imaginable. Sadly, the Caspian seal is classified as endangered: its population has fallen from over one million individuals a century ago to fewer than 100,000 today, due to pollution, hunting, and climate change.

The Przewalski's horse — known in Kazakh as "tarpan" — is the last truly wild horse species on Earth. Domestic horses are descended from horses that were tamed thousands of years ago, but the Przewalski's horse was never domesticated. It went extinct in the wild in the 1960s, but a remarkable international conservation programme reintroduced captive-bred horses back to the Kazakh steppe. Today, a small but growing population roams freely in the Altyn Emel National Park in Kazakhstan. Seeing these horses run across the open steppe is one of the most moving wildlife experiences imaginable.

Kazakhstan's diverse landscapes — from the frozen peaks of the Tian Shan to the sun-scorched dunes of the Kyzylkum Desert — also support thousands of plant species, reptiles, fish, and migratory birds. The country lies on one of the most important bird migration routes in Eurasia, and ornithologists from around the world visit every spring and autumn to observe species that travel between Siberia and South Asia. The wetlands of the Ili River delta are particularly important: they provide feeding grounds for hundreds of thousands of birds at a time.

Protecting Kazakhstan's extraordinary wildlife requires the work of dedicated rangers, scientists, and local communities. Organisations such as the Snow Leopard Trust, WWF Kazakhstan, and the Saiga Conservation Alliance work tirelessly to protect these species and the habitats they depend on. As future scientists, teachers, and citizens, WKU students have a role to play too. As Kamila wrote in her biology essay: "The most powerful thing a young person can do for nature is to first fall in love with it — and then fight to protect it." 🐆

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: Kamila, you're the biology fan — what's the most impressive animal in Kazakhstan, in your opinion?

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Without a doubt — the snow leopard. It's the most elusive and the most beautiful wild cat in Asia.

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: Really? I thought it was the saiga antelope — it's the oldest animal on the steppe, right?

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Yes! The saiga is older than the mammoth — over 2 million years! But it has the strangest nose I've ever seen.

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: Ha! What about birds? I know the steppe eagle is huge — bigger than most eagles in the world.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: It has a wingspan of over 2 metres! And it's one of the fastest divers — up to 250 km per hour.

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: That's incredible. Which is the most endangered one, though?

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: All of them are threatened. But the Caspian seal has had the steepest decline — from over a million to under 100,000.

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: That's terrible. What can we actually do to help?

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Learn about them, talk about them, support conservation charities. Awareness is the most important first step.

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: I had no idea Kazakhstan had such incredible wildlife. I feel guilty for never noticing it before.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: That's exactly why we study it! The most beautiful things in life are sometimes the least visible ones.

grammarNote:
Превосходная степень (superlative) используется когда мы говорим о САМОМ выдающемся предмете или человеке среди группы. В русском языке это "самый большой", "наиболее красивый". В английском — всегда с артиклем THE.

Формула: THE + прилагательное в превосходной степени

🔢 КАК ОБРАЗОВЫВАТЬ:

① Короткие прилагательные (1 слог) → THE + прилаг. + EST:
   big → the biggest · small → the smallest · old → the oldest
   tall → the tallest · fast → the fastest · cheap → the cheapest
   ⚠️ Удвоение согласной: big→bigg-est · hot→hott-est · thin→thinn-est

② Длинные прилагательные (2+ слога) → THE MOST + прилаг.:
   beautiful → the most beautiful · interesting → the most interesting
   expensive → the most expensive · comfortable → the most comfortable
   important → the most important · difficult → the most difficult

③ Исключения — запомни наизусть!
   good → the best · bad → the worst
   far → the furthest/farthest · little → the least

④ Двусложные на -y → THE + прилаг.(y→i) + EST:
   happy → the happiest · easy → the easiest · heavy → the heaviest

💡 Использование в предложениях:
"Charyn Canyon is the most spectacular landscape in Kazakhstan."
"Almaty is the biggest city, but Astana is the most modern."
"Summer is the hottest season in Uralsk — up to +40°C!"
"What is the most effective way to learn English?"
